summary_oneline: Make uvloop an optional, lazily-imported speedup; finish the Python 3.14 build; add Windows wheels to release.yml
summary: The request bundles three infrastructure changes. (1) uvloop is a hard runtime dependency on non-Windows platforms yet is never imported anywhere in the package, so it is pure install weight; the fix is to drop it from `dependencies`, expose it as an optional extra, and add a small helper that installs the uvloop policy only when the module is importable, mirroring the `HAS_RUST` fallback already used by `datamodel/rs_parsers/__init__.py`. (2) Python 3.14 is already present in classifiers, the release matrix (`cp314-*`), and the locked toolchain (Cython 3.2.9, PyO3 0.29); what remains is verifying the build end to end, tightening the Cython floor, and bumping Makefile/uv defaults. (3) Windows is blocked by two things only: GCC-specific flags in `setup.py` (`-O3`, `-lstdc++`) and a Linux-only cibuildwheel job in `release.yml` whose Rust pre-build step assumes bash, `/root/.cargo` and `.so` files. The Rust crate itself has no platform-specific code.

constraints.title: uvloop has no call site
constraints.statement: The package never imports uvloop or configures an event loop; 'automatic usage' must be a new, explicit helper, not a change to existing code.
constraints.implication: Design decision needed on where the helper lives and whether it runs on import (see U1).

constraints.title: Library must not hijack the caller's loop policy
constraints.statement: datamodel is a library consumed by other asyncio apps (asyncpg-based). Installing a global event loop policy at import time is a side effect that can break callers already using a different loop.
constraints.implication: Prefer an opt-in function (e.g. `install_uvloop()`) plus a documented env-var or explicit call; never auto-run at `import datamodel`.

constraints.title: GCC-only flags in setup.py
constraints.statement: `-O3` and `-lstdc++` are passed unconditionally; MSVC rejects `-lstdc++`.
constraints.implication: Flags must be selected per compiler (`sys.platform == 'win32'` → `/O2`, no libstdc++ link).

constraints.title: Rust pre-build step is bash/Linux-specific
constraints.statement: CIBW_BEFORE_BUILD uses `curl | sh`, `/root/.cargo/bin`, `/tmp/_rs` and filters `.so` only.
constraints.implication: Windows needs its own CIBW_BEFORE_BUILD_WINDOWS (rustup already present on GitHub runners) and `.pyd` extraction; package-data already accepts `*.pyd`.

constraints.title: Artifact naming collision
constraints.statement: Artifacts are named `wheels-py<version>`; a second OS in the matrix produces duplicate names.
constraints.implication: Rename to `wheels-<os>-py<version>` and keep the `wheels-*` download pattern.

constraints.title: 3.14 is mostly done
constraints.statement: Classifier, release matrix entry, PyO3 0.29 and Cython 3.2.9 are all in place; only verification and the `Cython>=3.0.11` floor remain.
constraints.implication: Scope 3.14 work as 'finish and verify', not 'add'.

constraints.title: No PR-time CI
constraints.statement: Only release.yml exists; a broken Windows or 3.14 build surfaces only when a release is cut.
constraints.implication: Consider a lightweight build-only workflow on PR, or at least `workflow_dispatch` on release.yml for dry runs.

constraints.title: Stale worktree
constraints.statement: `.claude/worktrees/migrate-uv-python314` is fully merged and 8 commits behind main.
constraints.implication: Remove it before starting a new worktree to avoid duplicate grep hits and confusion.

whats_new: A small optional-import helper (proposed `datamodel/libs/uvloop.py` or similar) exposing `HAS_UVLOOP` and an explicit `install_uvloop()`/`use_uvloop()` that sets the policy only if uvloop imports and the platform is not Windows.
`[project.optional-dependencies].uvloop` extra (and optionally a `speedups` umbrella) in pyproject.toml.
A `windows-latest` leg in the release matrix producing `cp310`–`cp314` win_amd64 wheels, with the Rust `.pyd` staged into `datamodel/rs_parsers/`.
A skip-if-missing pytest that exercises the uvloop helper.

select `/O2` on MSVC and drop `-lstdc++`; keep `-O3 -lstdc++` elsewhere

Making the Rust extension mandatory on Windows: `HAS_RUST=False` fallback stays acceptable if the .pyd build proves flaky.
Auto-installing uvloop at `import datamodel` time (rejected on library-hygiene grounds unless U1 says otherwise).
Removing other heavy dependencies (numpy, asyncpg, psycopg) — out of scope.
Rewriting tox.ini or adding a full PR test matrix (recommend, but separate).

confidence_map.claim: uvloop is declared but never imported; removing it is safe for the library and its tests
Python 3.14 is already wired into classifiers, the release matrix and the locked toolchain; remaining work is verification
The Windows blocker for the Cython layer is limited to the `-O3`/`-lstdc++` flags in setup.py
The Rust extension will build on windows-latest with MSVC without source changes
release.yml needs an OS matrix, a Windows-specific pre-build step, `.pyd` handling and OS-qualified artifact names
The right place for 'automatic usage' is an opt-in helper, not an import-time side effect
Ten Cython extensions compile cleanly under MSVC once flags are fixed (no POSIX-only C calls)
The stale migrate-uv-python314 worktree can be deleted safely

unknowns.question: Where should 'automatic usage' of uvloop take effect?
plausible_answers: a) opt-in helper `datamodel.libs.uvloop.install_uvloop()` that callers invoke explicitly (recommended)
b) helper plus an env var (e.g. DATAMODEL_USE_UVLOOP=1) checked at import
c) set the policy unconditionally at `import datamodel` when uvloop is importable

unknowns.question: Should uvloop be exposed as a pip extra, and under what name?
plausible_answers: c) no extra; users install uvloop themselves

unknowns.question: On Windows, must the Rust `.pyd` ship in the wheel, or is the pure-Python fallback (HAS_RUST=False) acceptable for the first release?
plausible_answers: a) ship the .pyd; fail the release if the Rust build fails
b) best-effort: build .pyd but allow fallback if maturin fails
c) Cython-only Windows wheels for now

unknowns.question: Should the same change add macOS (arm64/x86_64) wheels while the matrix is being restructured?
plausible_answers: a) no, Windows only as requested
b) yes, add macos-latest in the same matrix

overall_confidence_rationale: Localization and the 3.14/Windows CI facts are high-confidence and directly cited. Bounded to medium because the uvloop 'automatic usage' semantics are a design choice the codebase cannot answer (U1) and MSVC compilation of the Cython sources is untested (C7).

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization is high-confidence and the work decomposes cleanly into three independent tasks (uvloop extra + helper, MSVC flags + Windows CI leg, 3.14 verification). No architectural fork warrants a brainstorm; the only open design question (U1) can be fixed in the spec.

alternatives.when: if you want to compare uvloop integration strategies (helper vs env var vs import-time) before committing
not recommended: three separate surfaces (packaging, build flags, CI) are too broad for a single task
